tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

#!/bin/bash
# usage: axcheck.sh Module.Name [Module.Name ...]   (run after lake build of those modules)
SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref
F=$SP/axcheck_$$.lean
{
  echo "import Lean"
  for m in "$@"; do echo "import $m"; done
  echo 'open Lean Elab Command in'
  echo '#eval show Lean.Core.CoreM Unit from do'
  echo '  let env ← getEnv'
  printf '  for modName in [%s] do\n' "$(printf '`%s, ' "$@" | sed 's/, $//')"
  cat <<'L'
    let some mod := env.getModuleIdx? modName | throwError "no module"
    let mut all := 0
    let mut thms := 0
    let mut bad : Array (Name × Array Name) := #[]
    for (n, ci) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
      if env.getModuleIdxFor? n == some mod then
        all := all + 1
        if let .thmInfo _ := ci then thms := thms + 1
        let axs ← collectAxioms n
        let extra := axs.filter fun a => a != ``propext && a != ``Quot.sound
        if !extra.isEmpty then bad := bad.push (n, extra)
    IO.println s!"{modName}: constants {all}, theorems {thms}"
    IO.println s!"outside propext, Quot.sound: {bad}"
L
} > $F
cd /Users/guygouri/Devlab/ernlang/ern/formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake env lean $F
rm -f $F

# Reading policy for the reference kernel (fixed by the orchestrator; every item is reported for arbitration)

General
- The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.
- When a clause has no checkable content in the state (undefined term), do not invent content: omit it from the definition and record it in readings.md (clause, quote, why it cannot be formalized).
- When a clause has two readings, use the one listed below; if the case is not listed, use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings, and record it in readings.md with both readings and an example of a program whose verdict changes.
- A representation choice that changes no accepted program is free (record it briefly).

State (§38): S3 = (F, nF, P, I, A, D, dead, pin). No arena registry, no callParams, no freed. Library state lives elsewhere.
Outcomes (§58): one type Outcome3 σ := ok σ | reject | fail; every O1–O16 relation except alloc never yields fail.
O1 derive (§60): takes a region (List Nat, read extensionally), not a place. Preconditions: active source; ExercisableAt source mode; every leaf of region exists, is a leaf, belongs to afp source; mode ≤ effective mode of source on each leaf; §60.3 as a decidable clause (no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible); §60.4 current frame live. §60.1c "origin chain and anchors valid" and §60.4b "footprint and anchoring restrictions": no checkable content -> omitted, recorded.
O2 split (§61): draft clauses (incl. no exclusive right already distributed). §61.4 is NOT a precondition (the §61 note says an accepted split may violate I1 without DDSound) -> recorded.
O3 release (§62): draft clauses; §62.5 (abstraction contracts) omitted, recorded.
O4 transfer (§63): draft clauses MINUS the draft's extra clause "(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst" (not in §63); PLUS §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, as LockOptions.Opt2Transfer on formal/derivability_0.1); effect: dependencies follow the corresponding places corr(r) (not all to the destination root); §63.6 over moved usable places and AnchorOrder in the resulting state; §63.7 AnchorOrderHeld for the moved held authorities in the resulting state; §63.4 = draft ActiveDerivedOutside reading (recorded); §63.2 child order = place index order (recorded).
O5 depend (§64): draft clauses; §64.2b "real dependency" omitted, recorded.
O8 store (§65): draft clauses (they match).
O9/O10/O11 (§66–§68): add "every leaf belongs to a usable place" (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1); O10 keeps §67.2 explicitly.
O12 endUse (§69): death markers transitive over owned storage; drop the draft's extra disjunct that blocks descendants of authorities the step releases (not in §69.2) -> record the consequence.
O13 free (§70): death markers transitive; no extra "Usable p" and no clearing of D beyond what §70 prescribes; §70.4 scope = the released unit (place and storage that dies with it).
O14 alloc (§71): shape nonempty with exactly ONE root (one new storage root), parts' parents inside the shape, no owner component; provider clause as written in §71.2 (Modify OR writeShared over SharedMutable metadata) -> conflict with §36 recorded; outcomes reject / fail (not Satisfiable) / ok.
O6 enterFrame (§72): locals owned directly by the new frame (no local owned by another local); §72.3 ParamOriginHidden; §72.4 AnchorOrderHeld in the resulting state.
O7 exitFrame (§73): draft (first surviving active origin, held by a frame or a usable place).
O15/O16 pin/unpin (§74, §75): per-leaf dynamic pin flags (draft); unpin requires the place usable and K.ExternalDone(place) on the place; StaticPinnedBottom is a condition on (K, statics), not on states.
HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.
WF3 (§49): a structure with eight named fields, one per item:
 1 frames: F nonempty, no duplicates, every frame < nF;
 2 places: parent links valid and acyclic (representation: parent index < child index), parts share the owner and death marker of their parent;
 3 owners: owner frames < nF, owner places exist; "well-founded ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" read as stated for usable places (Usable is inductive) -> recorded with the global-acyclicity alternative;
 4 footprints: every footprint member is an existing leaf;
 5 authorities: origins exist and precede (origin index < id: representation of acyclic chains ending at a root);
 6 RootChain (draft);
 7 RootHeld as §49.7 states it: every usable root place has an active root authority, Modify, no origin, held by its owner, whose footprint is the place's footprint (draft RootLive + mode);
 8 holder validity (draft poss).
 The draft's converse RootHeld (every origin-less authority covering a leaf of root r is held by r's owner) is NOT a WF3 clause: keep it as a separate auxiliary predicate.
I2 (§51): mode conservation unconditional (not under ∀ p ∈ footprint).
Initial state (§47): base frame 0; statics may be owned by statics; root authority held by the owner. Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.
Reachable: closure of S3.init statics under the kernel steps O1–O16 only.

# Fix round 1: kernel (KM-1, KM-2)

Branch `reference/memory-model-v0`. Nothing is committed. The full project builds with
`lake build` in `formal/` and prints no warnings. The forbidden-token grep prints nothing.
`axcheck.sh` prints empty lists for every touched module: Access.Lemmas, Access.Main,
Preserve.{Alloc, DeriveSplitRelease, EndFree, Frames, Small, Transfer} and Lib.HandlePool.

## KM-2: KAux removed from the per-step obligation (fixed)

The defect: `KAux = RootHeldConv` is not a clause of §49 or §57. It was a hypothesis of every
per-operation `*_preserves`, of `op_preserves`/`kstep_preserves` and of `exitFrame_no_dangling`.

### New lemma

`Lemmas.lean`: `rootHeldConv_active` (§49.4, §49.7, §50, §54). It derives the active, origin-less
fragment of `RootHeldConv` from `WF3 ∧ I1 ∧ NoDangling`. It is the reviewer's `conv_active`
(review2/main-preserve/kaux2.lean).

### Hypothesis replaced by I1 (a §57 clause)

The proofs applied `RootHeldConv` only to an active authority with no origin.

| Theorem | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `EndFree.endUse_noDangling` | `WF3 → NoDangling → RootHeldConv → …` | `WF3 → NoDangling → I1 → …` |
| `EndFree.free_noDangling` | same | same |
| `Frames.exit_noDangling` | `WF3 → NoDangling → RootHeldConv → OriginsSurvive → …` | `WF3 → I1 → NoDangling → OriginsSurvive → …` |
| `exitFrame_no_dangling` | `WF3 s → NoDangling s → RootHeldConv s → ExitStep … → …` | `WF3 s → I1 s → NoDangling s → ExitStep … → …` (§57 clauses only). The docstring says so. |

### Per-operation preservation: KInv split from KAux

Every operation now has `X_preserves : KInv s → step ok → KInv s'` with no `KAux` (`split` also
takes `DDSound`). The auxiliary part is a separate theorem:

| Operation | `KInv` theorem (restated) | `KAux` theorem |
|---|---|---|
| derive, split, release | `derive_/split_/release_preserves` | existing `*_preserves_rootHeldConv` (step level) |
| depend, store | `depend_/store_preserves` | existing `*_preserves_rootHeldConv` |
| read, write, writeShared, pin, unpin | `*_preserves` | new `*_preserves_kAux (haux : KAux s) (h) : KAux s'` |
| endUse, free | `endUse_/free_preserves` | new `endUse_/free_preserves_kAux` |
| enter | `enter_preserves` | new `enter_preserves_kAux (hk : KInv s) (ha : KAux s) (h)` (needs `WF3`) |
| exit | `exit_preserves` | new `exit_preserves_kAux (ha : KAux s) (h)` |
| alloc | `alloc_preserves` | new `alloc_preserves_kAux (hk : KInv s) (ha : KAux s) (h)` (needs `WF3`) |

- `op_preserves`: `DDSound k → KInv s → op.Step k s (.ok s') → op ≠ transfer → KInv s'`. This is

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Lemmas

/-!
# Access kernel: the preserved invariant

The conjunction that every kernel step must preserve (§57) and the auxiliary invariant carried
with it. The per-operation preservation modules state their results with these two predicates.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-- The kernel invariant of §57: `WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan`. -/
def KInv (s : S3) : Prop := WF3 s ∧ Inv3 s ∧ AnchorOrderHeld s ∧ NoOrphan s

/-- Auxiliary invariant carried with `KInv` (§40, §49.7): the converse root-holder property
`RootHeldConv`, which is not a clause of `WF3`. -/
def KAux (s : S3) : Prop := RootHeldConv s

/-- `NoOrphan` follows from `WF3` (§54, §49.7), so `KInv` reduces to its first three
conjuncts. -/
theorem kInv_of {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (hi : Inv3 s) (ha : AnchorOrderHeld s) : KInv s :=
  ⟨hw, hi, ha, noOrphan_of_wf3 hw⟩

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access
/-- `RootHeld` (§49.7, §40): every usable root place has an active root authority of own mode
`Modify`, with no origin, held by the owner of the place, whose footprint is the footprint of the
place. -/
def RootHeld (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ r, RootPlace s.P r → s.Usable r → ∃ (i : Nat) (z : Authority) (pr : Place),
    s.A[i]? = some z ∧ z.active = true ∧ z.origin = none ∧ z.mode = .modify ∧
    s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner ∧ ∀ l, l ∈ z.footprint ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P r

/-- Auxiliary converse of `RootHeld` (§40, §49.7), not a clause of `WF3`: an authority with no
origin is held by the owner of the root place of every leaf it covers. -/
def RootHeldConv (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Nat) (z : Authority) (l r : Nat), s.A[x]? = some z → z.origin = none → l ∈ z.footprint →
    RootPlace s.P r → partOf s.P l r → ∃ pr, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner

/-! ## `WF3` (§49) -/

/-- `WF3(s)` (§49): one field per item of §49. Index order of parents and origins represents
acyclicity (§49, last paragraph). -/
structure WF3 (s : S3) : Prop where
  /-- §49.1: the stack is nonempty and duplicate-free, every frame below `nF`. -/
  frames : s.F ≠ [] ∧ s.F.Nodup ∧ ∀ f ∈ s.F, f < s.nF
  /-- §49.2: parent links are valid and acyclic (the parent precedes the child); a part shares
  its parent's owner and death marker. -/
  places : ∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (r : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.parent = some r →
    ∃ pr : Place, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ r < q ∧ pr.owner = pl.owner ∧ s.dead r = s.dead q
  /-- §49.3: owner frames are below `nF`; owner places exist; the ownership chain of every usable
  place is finite and reaches a live frame. -/
  owners : (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (f : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .frame f →
      f < s.nF) ∧
    (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (o : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o →
      o < s.P.length) ∧
    ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∃ f, FrameOf s q f ∧ f ∈ s.F

theorem XReach.kseq {k : K} {statics : Statics} {s s' : S3} (hr : XReach k statics s)
    (h : KSeq k s s') : XReach k statics s' := by
  induction h with
  | refl => exact hr
  | tail _ hs ih => exact .step ih (.kernel hs)

/-- The guarantee of §57 on the kernel side of library runs (HandlePool v0.4 annex): `KInv` on
every state reached by kernel steps O1–O16 and ends of slot contents. It is not a clause of the
contract and is not proved here: `xreach_inv` reduces it to the preservation of `KInv ∧ KAux` by
every kernel step, which the transfer of §63 breaks (`transfer_breaks_kinv`). -/
def KernelGuarantee (k : K) (statics : Statics) : Prop := ∀ s, XReach k statics s → KInv s

/-- A library step from a kernel state in `XReach` lands in `XReach`, under `KInv` (§57;
HandlePool v0.4 annex). -/
theorem xreach_pstep {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L L' : PState}
    (hr : XReach k statics L.kern) (hk : KInv L.kern) (hs : PStep k L L') :
    XReach k statics L'.kern := by
  rcases pstep_kernel hk hs with h | ⟨q, i, hpre, he⟩
  · exact hr.kseq h
  · rw [he]; exact .step hr (.contentEnd hpre)

/-- The kernel state of every library-reachable state is reached from `S3.init statics` by kernel
steps O1–O16 and ends of slot contents (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex), given `KInv` on such
states. -/
theorem pReach_xreach {k : K} {statics : Statics} (hX : KernelGuarantee k statics)
    {L : PState} (h : PReach k statics L) : XReach k statics L.kern := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact .init
  | step _ hs ih => exact xreach_pstep ih (hX _ ih) hs

/-- `KInv ∧ KAux` (§57) holds on every state reached by kernel steps and ends of slot contents,
when it holds initially and every kernel step O1–O16 preserves it (`contentEnd_preserves` and
`contentEnd_preserves_kAux` cover the ends of slot contents; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3). -/
theorem xreach_inv {k : K} {statics : Statics}
    (h0 : KInv (S3.init statics) ∧ KAux (S3.init statics))
    (hK : ∀ s s', KInv s → KAux s → KStep k s s' → KInv s' ∧ KAux s') {s : S3}
    (h : XReach k statics s) : KInv s ∧ KAux s := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact h0
  | step _ hs ih =>
    cases hs with
    | kernel hs => exact hK _ _ ih.1 ih.2 hs
    | contentEnd hpre => exact ⟨contentEnd_preserves ih.1 hpre, contentEnd_preserves_kAux ih.2⟩
    (∃ L', ResolveManyStep K0 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩] .observe w4 (.ok L') ∧ PReachI K0 hst L' ∧
      L'.res = [⟨0, 3, 4, .observe, [(5, 0, 0), (6, 0, 0)]⟩]) ∧
    ∀ o, ResolveManyStep K0 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩] .modify w4 o → o = .fail := by
  have hok : ResolveManyStep K0 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩] .observe w4 (.ok _) :=
    .ok (pl := pl4) rfl (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
  exact ⟨⟨_, hok, .step w4_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 (.resolveMany hok), rfl⟩,
    (pool_resolveMany_distinct (L' := w4) (pl := pl4)).1 rfl (by decide) (by decide)⟩

/-- `freeSlot` is not a kernel `endUse` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "Le contrôle n'interprète pas
`internal` comme un emprunt externe"; §69.2): on `w4`, `freeSlot(⟨0, 0, 0⟩)` is accepted, while the
kernel `endUse` of slot place 1 is rejected, because `internal` (authority 3, derived, active,
covering place 1) is held by the pool value outside the slot. Both states satisfy `KInv ∧ KAux`
(§57), decided through `Arena.KInvB`. -/
theorem freeSlot_not_endUse :
    (∃ L', FreeSlotStep K0 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ w4 (.ok L') ∧ PReachI K0 hst L' ∧
      KInv L'.kern ∧ KAux L'.kern) ∧
      ¬ EndUsePre K0 w4.kern 1 ∧ KInv w4.kern ∧ KAux w4.kern := by
  have hok : FreeSlotStep K0 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ w4 (.ok _) :=
    .ok (pl := pl4) (sl := ⟨1, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)
  have hk4 : KInv w4.kern ∧ KAux w4.kern := Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)
  exact ⟨⟨_, hok, .step w4_reach hk4.1 (.freeSlot hok), Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)⟩, by decide,
    hk4⟩

content.content:
# Annexe D — Instance `HandlePool` (non normative, contrat de bibliothèque)

Cette annexe décrit une **instance de bibliothèque** de la discipline MM-03, et non une nouvelle opération primitive du langage. Les noms sont sémantiques. Le contrat doit être reconstruit et vérifié ; les résultats du jalon 3 concernent le modèle exploratoire et ses conditions, **pas** automatiquement les règles corrigées ci-dessous.

## D.1 — Identité, état et stockage

Un handle est une donnée `(poolId, slot, gen)` **sans autorité d'accès intrinsèque**. L'identité logique `poolId` est fraîche et n'est pas réutilisée pendant l'exécution pertinente : détruire puis recréer un pool à la même adresse ne réactive pas un ancien handle. Chaque pool vivant conserve une entrée abstraite `{storage, internal, slots}`, où chaque slot possède `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`. Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage` ; leur métadonnée abstraite est représentée en octets par l'implémentation de bibliothèque.

`storage` peut être local, statique, alloué ou être un bloc issu d'une arène. **`newPool(storage, internal)` exige que toutes les feuilles du stockage d'entrée soient `Uninit`** et doit vérifier la garde unifiée de MM-03.3 §2.7 bis sur les deux registres des abstractions vivantes. Il reprend les autres obligations applicables de `newArena` sans fabriquer ni droits ni initialisation des valeurs de slots. Les entrées libres sont `Uninit` ; leur génération initiale est zéro. Une autorité ne peut être `internal` de deux abstractions vivantes, et une arène ne peut réutiliser l'`internal` d'un pool vivant.

## D.2 — Emprunt composé et résolution

Une résolution réussie dérive **de `internal` une autorité compagne** couvrant toutes les feuilles du stockage du pool, de mode `Observe` ou `Modify`, puis dérive **de cette compagne** une autorité de même mode par entrée résolue. L'autorité d'entrée est une descendante de la compagne, et non une autre dérivation indépendante de `internal`. Les deux sont soumises aux règles ordinaires de modes effectifs, d'exercice, de détention, d'ancrage et de transfert ; aucune permission nouvelle n'est créée.

`resolve(h, Observe | Modify)` vérifie l'identité de pool, la génération et la vivacité du slot **avant toute création d'autorité** : handle d'un autre pool, périmé, slot absent ou libre ⇒ `fail`, sans changement d'état. Une résolution valide exige l'exercice légal de `internal` au mode requis. Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool ; des compagnes `Observe` peuvent coexister. Il est impossible de libérer une compagne tant que ses descendantes d'entrée sont actives (O3.2). La propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau, pas seulement deux appels successifs de `resolve`.

`resolveMany(handles, Modify)` crée **une** compagne `Modify` et une autorité `Modify` par entrée. La distinction des slots est vérifiée dynamiquement pour ce lot ; toute identité invalide, génération périmée, entrée libre ou répétition de slot donne `fail` **atomique**, sans création partielle de droits. `resolveMany(handles, Observe)` utilise des dérivations `Observe` de la compagne `Observe`, **sans `split` ni contrôle de distinction** : la répétition du même handle valide est permise. Les `reject` de discipline d'accès restent distincts des `fail` de validation des handles.

`unresolve` libère d'abord toutes les dérivées d'entrée encore actives, puis la compagne. Les règles de `release`, y compris celles qui empêchent la libération en présence de descendants ou d'ancres valides, restent applicables ; le contrat ne supprime pas silencieusement des autorités transférées.

## D.3 — Allocation et fin d'usage de slot

`allocSlot(pool, dst)` exige un pool vivant, l'autorisation d'administration de ses métadonnées, une destination utilisable et libre d'autorité active, non `Init`, apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle. `fail` si aucun slot libre ; `ok` choisit un slot libre, le rend vivant, conserve sa génération et écrit son handle dans la seule feuille `dst`, selon les obligations de représentation (Spec 4) et d'ABI (Spec 11). **Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit`** jusqu'à son écriture ; l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot.

`freeSlot(h)` exige un pool **vivant** et `MetaRight`, c'est-à-dire le droit légal d'administration de la valeur pool par `Modify` exerçable ou par mutation `writeShared` admissible de ses métadonnées `SharedMutable`. `fail` si l'identité ou la génération ne correspond pas ; un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité. Pour réussir, la fin logique du contenu doit être admissible : **aucune dépendance utilisable** ne serait invalidée, **aucune feuille n'est épinglée**, et **aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres**. En particulier, aucune descendante active d'une compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée. Le contrôle n'interprète pas `internal` comme un emprunt externe empêchant systématiquement le nettoyage de ses propres slots.

L'effet `ok` applique au **contenu** les effets de fin d'usage d'`endUse`, remet les feuilles de l'entrée à `Uninit`, marque l'entrée libre et incrémente sa génération ; **il ne désalloue pas implicitement l'allocation MM-02 du stockage**. Il ne s'agit pas de supposer une invocation de O12 autorisée par simple `MetaRight` : la correspondance des effets et la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constituent une **obligation explicite de reconstruction**, notamment dans les cas `writeShared`.

## D.4 — Invariant corrigé et limites

`PoolInv` exige : (1) les entrées sont deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; (2) aucune autorité d'entrée active ne désigne un slot libre ou une ancienne génération (`pool_no_stale_access`) ; (3) **garantie de transition** : `freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné. La dernière clause concerne le succès des transitions, non une interdiction globale de toutes les dérivations du noyau sur des slots libres. Les dérivations ordinaires issues d'une autorité d'entrée restent permises par le noyau.

Les générations sont des entiers naturels dans le modèle abstrait. Leur débordement ou leur recyclage dans une représentation finie doivent être empêchés par l'implémentation (par exemple retrait définitif d'un slot) ; l'ABI est spécifiée en Spec 11. L'encapsulation qui empêche un client d'accéder directement à une compagne administrative appartient à la Spec 9. Les handles persistants peuvent représenter des liens cycliques ; les résolutions qui en découlent restent temporaires et soumises à MM-03.

**Statut des preuves :** le jalon 3 rapporte `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`, `pool_no_stale_access`, `pool_resolveMany_atomic`, `pool_resolveMany_distinct`, `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` et `pool_entries_disjoint` sur son brouillon, sous les hypothèses détaillées dans `J3_v0.1.md`. Il rapporte également un contre-exemple à l'ancienne formulation de `pool_inv_preserved`. **Il ne constitue pas encore la preuve** de la nouvelle règle `freeSlot` sous `MetaRight` ni de la totalité du contrat corrigé : ces obligations sont consignées en annexe F.

# Annexe E — Registre inter-spécifications (non normatif pour la Spec 1)

| Destination | Obligations ouvertes ou précisées |
|---|---|
| **Spec 2 — Concurrence** | Partie concurrente de `stat` ; `writeShared` et synchronisation ; transférabilité, partageabilité, suspension concurrente ; cas H39, H41. |
| **Spec 3 — Contrôle de flux et appels** | Protection forte de paramètres (`Reach`, `lineage`, `derivedIn`, G1', A3 strict) ; ré-emprunt d'un paramètre `Modify` par un paramètre dérivé `Observe` (H01, admis dans le noyau séquentiel, sans promettre la protection forte) ; **passage par valeur (`sink`) vers l'appelé** : prévoir la primitive MM-03 correspondante, transfert d'un emplacement de l'appelant vers un local de l'appelé au moment de l'entrée, sans affaiblir arbitrairement O4 ; retour et `defer` (H16, H27b, H38, H40, H42). |
| **Spec 4 — Types** | Validité de représentation (`dec`), `SameSizeAlong`, information de forme pour des régions non contiguës, feuille de destination d'une référence typée, correspondance `kind` et type ; **mémoire rendue par une abstraction de réutilisation (bloc d'arène réémis, entrée de pool) exposée comme typée non initialisée jusqu'à écriture explicite**, sans réinterprétation implicite d'anciens octets. La décision ne change pas rétroactivement les effets d'initialisation de `reset` sur l'état abstrait MM-03. |
| **Spec 9 — Encapsulation** | Empêcher l'usage extérieur des autorités internes/compagnes administratives des bibliothèques sûres. |

/-- One `ok` step of a library run (HandlePool v0.4 annex; non-normative library contract): a
kernel step O1–O16 of non-administrative code, the registry unchanged, or an accepted pool
operation (§57, §58). -/
inductive PStep (k : K) : PState → PState → Prop where
  | kernel {L : PState} {s' : S3} : KStep k L.kern s' → PStep k L { L with kern := s' }
  | newPool {L L' : PState} {others : List (List Nat)} {st i : Nat} :
      NewPoolStep others st i L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | allocSlot {L L' : PState} {j dst : Nat} : AllocSlotStep j dst L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | resolve {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} {m : Mode} :
      ResolveStep j h m L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | resolveMany {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {hs : List Handle} {m : Mode} :
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | unresolve {L L' : PState} {c : Nat} : UnresolveStep c L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | freeSlot {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
      PStep k L L'

def I3Check (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q < s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, s.Active x

/-- Bounded `RootHeldConv` for one authority (§40, §49.7). -/
def RootConvOK (s : S3) (z : Authority) : Prop :=
  z.origin = none → ∀ l ∈ z.footprint, ∀ r < s.P.length, RootPlace s.P r → partOf s.P l r →
    OptP (s.P[r]?) (fun pr => z.holder = pr.owner) False

/-- Decidability of `RootConvOK` (§49.7). -/
instance (s : S3) (z : Authority) : Decidable (RootConvOK s z) := by
  unfold RootConvOK; infer_instance

/-- Bounded `RootHeldConv` (§40, §49.7). -/
def RootHeldConvCheck (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ x < s.A.length, OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun z => RootConvOK s z) True

/-- Decidability of the bounded clauses (§50). -/
instance (s : S3) : Decidable (I1Check s) := by unfold I1Check; infer_instance
/-- Decidability of the bounded clauses (§51). -/
instance (s : S3) : Decidable (I2Check s) := by unfold I2Check; infer_instance
/-- Decidability of the bounded clauses (§52). -/
instance (s : S3) : Decidable (I3Check s) := by unfold I3Check; infer_instance
/-- Decidability of the bounded clauses (§49.7). -/
instance (s : S3) : Decidable (RootHeldConvCheck s) := by unfold RootHeldConvCheck; infer_instance

/-- The bounded checks imply `KInv` (§57) and `KAux` (§49.7). -/
theorem kInv_kAux_of_check {s : S3} (hw : WF3Check s) (h1 : I1Check s) (h2 : I2Check s)
    (h3 : I3Check s) (ho : AnchorOrder s) (hnd : NoDanglingCheck s) (hoh : AnchorOrderHeld s)
    (hc : RootHeldConvCheck s) : KInv s ∧ KAux s := by
  refine ⟨kInv_of (wf3_of_check hw) ⟨⟨?_, ?_, ?_, i4_always s⟩, ho, noDangling_of_check hnd⟩ hoh,
    ?_⟩
  · intro a b x y p hab ha hb xa ya hpx hpy hba hab'
    have h := h1 a (lt_of_getElem? ha) b (lt_of_getElem? hb) hab
    rw [ha] at h; simp only [OptP] at h; rw [hb] at h
    exact h xa ya ⟨p, hpx, hpy⟩ hba hab'
  · intro b y a hb hy
    have h := optP_of hb (h2 b (lt_of_getElem? hb))
    unfold OriginOK at h
    rw [hy] at h; simp only [OptP] at h
    cases hx : s.A[a]? with
    | none => rw [hx] at h; exact h.elim
    | some x => rw [hx] at h; exact ⟨x, rfl, h⟩
  · intro q hq x hx
    exact h3 q hq.lt hq x hx
  · intro x z l r hx hzo hl hr hlr
    have h := optP_of hx (hc x (lt_of_getElem? hx)) hzo l hl r hr.1 hr hlr
    cases hpr : s.P[r]? with
    | none => rw [hpr] at h; exact h.elim
    | some pr => rw [hpr] at h; exact ⟨pr, rfl, h⟩

content.content:
exact ⟨y, by rw [endUseEff, EndFree.cleanup_get, EndFree.endUseS_get, hy]; simp [hnh, hl], ya⟩

/-- The end of the content preserves `NoDangling` (§54, §69; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3), under
`WF3` (§49) and `I1` (§50): an active authority on a leaf of a place that stops being usable is
derived, and blocked by §69.2 on dying storage, or a root, held by the owner of the root place of
the leaf (`rootHeldConv_active`), which stays usable. -/
theorem contentEnd_noDangling {k : K} {s : S3} {q i : Nat} (hw : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s)
    (h1 : I1 s) (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) (hw' : WF3 (endUseEff s q)) :
    NoDangling (endUseEff s q) := by

/-- The end of the content of a slot place `q` under `ContentEndPre` preserves the kernel invariant
`KInv` (§57) (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constitue
une obligation explicite"; §69 effect); the auxiliary `KAux` is preserved by
`contentEnd_preserves_kAux`. -/
theorem contentEnd_preserves {k : K} {s : S3} {q i : Nat} (hk : KInv s)
    (hpre : ContentEndPre k s q i) : KInv (endUseEff s q) := by
      fun l hl => by rw [heff l hl]; exact Arena.allows_some_modify _⟩⟩

/-- An accepted `freeSlot` preserves the kernel invariant `KInv` (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3:
"la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constitue une obligation explicite"); the auxiliary
`KAux` is preserved by `freeSlot_preserves_kAux`. -/
theorem freeSlot_preserves {k : K} {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} (hk : KInv L.kern)
    (hst : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L')) : KInv L'.kern := by
`Modify` and with one `Observe` derive per handle (O1) in `Observe`; `unresolve` releases (O3).
`freeSlot` applies the effect function of O12 (§69) to the slot content under preconditions that
exempt `internal` and its ancestors (`ContentEndPre`): it is not a kernel `endUse` step.
`contentEnd_preserves` proves that it preserves `KInv` (§57), and `contentEnd_preserves_kAux` that
it preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (not a clause of §57); `pstep_kernel` states what every pool step
is on the kernel side.
